Entity Service Design Package Appendix P Runbook Template Instructions

This is a template for Appendix P Runbook of the Entity Service Design Package (SDP).

Refer to the following guidelines:

* Update this template with project-specific information.
* Complete the template content specified in brackets and then remove the brackets. For example, replace [Project Name] with the name of the project. You can perform a search and replace using the drop-down menu in the search box or **Ctrl+H** on your keyboard.
* Use the search box or **Ctrl+F** on your keyboard to make sure that all brackets are processed.
* To access and apply styles, use the Styles section on the Home tab or **Ctrl+Alt+Shift+S** on your keyboard.
* Remove all template instructions, including this Template Instructions page.
* Include this content in the full SDP document.

This template is owned by the Platform and Technical Architecture Discipline. It is part of the Design, Build, Test, Operational Readiness and Cutover, and Stabilization phases.

The template is aligned to Gainwell*One* Leading Practices.

* + - 1. Application Access

The purpose of the documentation contained in this section is to describe different activities related to [Application] ID provisioning and how they are routed and handled within the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol-Active Directory (LDAP-AD) for [Application].

* + - 1. ID Provisioning

The [Application] user’s account are created in LDAP-AD. LDAP provides a means to manage user and group membership stored in Active Directory. LDAP is a protocol to authenticate and authorize access to [Application] IT resources, while Active Directory is a database of user and group information. The process for creating a user account starts with creating a ServiceNow ticket in [Information System Acronym] [Project Acronym]. The user account is then be created by a Solution Architect.

LDAP ID Provisioning steps:

1. The [Application] Project Manager requests a User ID to be created in LDAP with the following information:

* User first and last name
* User Email address
* User domain ID (Global Pass account ID)
* Title
* Location

1. The Provisioning team creates the user in AD as an LDAP account.
2. Once the User ID is created, the confirmation is sent back to the Project Manager and cc’d to the user.
3. The User ID Provisioning team sends the User ID and password to the user.
4. The [Application] business team provides the [Application] business team Administrator with the User ID, group, and access rights request for confirmation (not password).
5. The [Application] business team Administrator checks the account management in [Application] to confirm the correct LDAP group is applied to the user.
   * + - 1. Account Decommissioning

LDAP Account Decommissioning steps:

1. The Project Manager requests that the user LDAP account be removed from AD. The Provisioning team provides the exact steps.
2. Once the LDAP account is removed from AD, the Provisioning team notifies the Project Manager.
3. The Project Manager notifies the [Application] business team Administrator to confirm the user is decommissioned from AD.
4. The ACM business team Administrator confirms in [Application] that the user’s LDAP account has been disabled due to the removal/disablement of the LDAP account from AD. The user ID remains in [Application] for auditing purposes but will not be removed. The user is simply disabled in [Application] once the AD decommissioning is complete.
   * + 1. User Account Updates

A user needing to update the account information can go to Adobe’s Client Console Desktop Application My account and click on My Profile. It shows the account information saved when the account was set up. If something needs to be changed, the user can access this page to make changes.

* + - 1. User Password Rules and Reset

[Information System Acronym] [Project Acronym]-managed [Application] User Repository and Policies:

* Must be at least eight characters for users and 12 characters for admins and no more than 25 characters
* Cannot contain “password,” “123456,” “654321,” or the username
* Must be composed of characters from at least three of the following four groups from the standard keyboard: uppercase, lowercase, numeric, or special characters
* Password expires every 45 days

Users who have forgotten their password can request their passwords to be reset by clicking the “I forgot my password” link. An email will be sent to the email address on record for the account with instructions on how to reset the password. The end user submits/opens a service ticket with the [Information System Acronym] [Project Acronym] Help Desk for password reset.

* + 1. CRM Data Loads

ACM pulls provider data from CRM on a daily basis. This is accomplished daily in the morning loads that run from 6:00 A.M. to 7:00 A.M. depending on the amount of data. Typically, it runs in about 15 minutes. The CRM connector pulls the data greater or equal to the last load data/time. This is the logic developed within the daily load workflows.

If there are issues with the data load, the Administrator will be notified. The load will be restarted or remediated at that time. No cleanup is required if there is a data load failure. In the event of a data load failure, the job can either be restarted or resumed with the next day’s cycle. The data and system will continue to be available.

Note: Data loads should not be restarted during the business hours, as this will impact CRM performance.

   1. Startup/Shutdown Procedures

The [Application] is leveraging the [Information System Acronym] Business Operations service. These tasks will remain as part of the responsibilities of the [Information System Acronym] Business Operations.

* + 1. System Startup

The [Application] is automatically started whenever the servers are restarted. There is no need for manual or human intervention. Moreover, the [Application] application is not monitored 24/7; it will be only monitored during business hours by SiteScope. The [Application] Administrator will be alerted in the event the application services fail, which triggers alerts from site scope monitoring. The [Application] Administrator will clear the alert and problem to bring the [Application] back online.

* + 1. System Shutdown

If the [Application] needs to be shut down for any reason, including maintenance, this can be achieved by either shutting down the IIS Web Server or the Operating System. The type of shut down needed depends on the type of maintenance needed. If the [Project Acronym] determines that there is a need to disable the [Application], [Information System Acronym] [Project Acronym] coordinates with the [Application] technical support team.
